MP:001.title: Marketing strategy
MP:001.pt: Explain the concept of marketing strategies

scenes.sub: What it is, the two parts it’s built from, and how it shows up on the exam
scenes.cap: A one-minute look at a concept that runs through the Marketing exam.

scenes.text: A business’s plan for reaching its marketing goals by choosing a target market and building a marketing mix to satisfy it.
scenes.cap: Define it first: a strategy is a plan, and it has two parts.

scenes.text: The specific group of customers the business decides to serve.
scenes.cap: No business can serve everyone well, so it chooses whom to focus on.

items.d: What is sold: features, brand name, packaging and services
What customers pay, including discounts and payment terms
Where and how customers get it: stores, websites, delivery
How customers learn about it: ads, social media, personal selling

scenes.cap: These four Ps are the tools the business controls.
Every P is chosen to fit the target market, and the four work together: change one, and the others may need to change too.

rows: Students who want a quick breakfast before class
Next to E117, on the way to class
scenes.cap: Every decision points back to the same group of customers.

a.d: What the business wants to achieve, such as growing its market share from 12% to 15%

b.d: How it will get there: the target market it serves and the marketing mix it uses

scenes.cap: When a question describes a number to reach, that target is a goal, not the strategy itself.

scenes.h: Sorting a decision into the mix
scenes.cap: Ask what the decision changes, and the P usually follows.

FI:238.title: Time value of money
FI:238.pt: Calculate the time value of money

scenes.sub: Why a dollar today is worth more than a dollar later, and how to calculate it
scenes.cap: Have the calculator ready: this concept is mostly math.

scenes.text: The idea that money available now is worth more than the same amount later, because money on hand today can earn interest.
scenes.cap: Define it first: time plus interest changes what money is worth.
Each year’s interest also earns interest, so the growth gets bigger every year.
PV is the amount today, r is the rate per period and n is the number of periods.

scenes.h: Interest more than once a year
scenes.cap: Divide the rate, and multiply the years, by the number of periods per year.

lines: Goal: $5,000 in 5 years at 12%, compounded quarterly
scenes.cap: To find what to deposit today, divide instead of multiply.

items: Compounded once a year instead of quarterly
scenes.cap: Check whether the answer should be larger (future value) or smaller (present value).
